tasks.short: Plan the programme season for target groups, write programme texts and the newsletter, send it, take sign-ups, and deliver programmes such as storytelling and sessions for special groups.

steps.what: Librarian plans client-centered programs for children, corporate clients and special groups
Librarian writes the programme texts and the newsletter

loop.input: The programme calendar entries with title, audience, date, place and a short note.
loop.output: Short programme texts and a newsletter draft.
loop.check: Dates, times and places are filled from the calendar fields by code, not by the model; the librarian edits every text.
loop.stop: Approved by the librarian, or after two redrafts the librarian writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Texts need wording per audience; a template only fills the facts.

steps.what: Librarian sends the newsletter to subscribers
Visitors sign up for programmes at the desk or by phone
Librarian takes sign-ups and keeps the attendee lists
Librarian delivers programmes such as storytelling for children and sessions for special groups

tasks.design: Programmes are entered once in the event calendar of the library website ({CMS}), which fills dates and places into texts. A bounded step drafts programme texts and the newsletter, the librarian edits them, and only the checked newsletter goes to subscribers. Visitors sign up online, which builds the attendee lists; desk and phone sign-ups go into the same calendar. Planning and delivering programmes stay with the librarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Texts were written from scratch and sign-ups kept on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Website event calendars take online sign-ups; language models draft short texts from fields.
tasks.still_hard: Older visitors and some groups keep signing up in person.
tasks.human_edge: Holding a room of toddlers with a story.
tasks.altitude: The librarian edits drafted texts instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether online sign-ups cut desk queues.

evidence.claim: Website event calendars take online sign-ups and build attendee lists.
Newsletters need subscribers' consent under the e-privacy rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from user needs to delivered programmes; programme budgets are outside.
Input contract: programme calendar kept by the librarian; subscriber list from the newsletter sign-up; fallback is paper lists.
Visitors sign up online instead of at the desk; about the same time, priced as customer time.
Planning and delivering do not change.
research_questions: Does attendance rise with online sign-up?

incremental.description: Librarian enters desk sign-ups in the calendar.
Visitors sign up online instead of at the desk.

approvals.approved_version: The newsletter as edited and checked by the librarian in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most visitors sign up in person; high: most sign up online and texts need light edits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: List available materials per subject and level, confer with teachers to select course materials and training aids, check copies, and reserve the chosen materials for the class.

steps.what: Librarian lists available materials per subject and grade level
Librarian confers with teachers to select course materials and training aids for particular grade levels
Librarian checks copies available for the class
Librarian reserves the chosen materials for the class

tasks.design: The library catalogue ({OTHER}) is tagged by subject and grade level, so saved searches give a material list per course with copies available. After conferring with the teacher, the librarian reserves the chosen set for the class in the same system instead of on a paper list. Conferring stays with the librarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lists were built by browsing shelves and catalogue screens, and reservations kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogues support level tags, saved searches and class reservations.
tasks.still_hard: Level tags are only as good as the cataloguing behind them.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which book a hesitant class will actually read.

reach.learn: Whether level lists widen the reading choice.

evidence.claim: Library catalogues support subject and level tags, saved searches and class reservations.

assumptions: Boundary: from course topics to the class reservation; buying new materials is outside.
Input contract: course topics from the teachers; level tags kept by the cataloguer; fallback is browsing and paper lists.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few items carry level tags yet; high: most of the collection is tagged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read committee papers, prepare the library's input and figures, represent the library in committee meetings and report back to staff.

steps.what: Librarian reads the committee papers
Librarian prepares the library's input and figures
Librarian represents the library on internal and external committees
Librarian reports back to library staff in the team meeting

tasks.design: Figures for committee input come from the library system's usage dashboard ({OTHER}) instead of a spreadsheet. Reading papers, representing the library and reporting back stay with the librarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were rebuilt in a spreadsheet for each committee.
tasks.enabler_now: Library systems offer standing usage dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Committee work is persuasion, which no tool does.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the library onto the agenda before decisions are made.

reach.learn: Whether standing figures strengthen the library's case.

evidence.claim: Library systems offer standing usage dashboards.

assumptions: Boundary: from committee papers to staff informed; carrying out committee decisions is outside.
Input contract: papers from the committee secretary; figures from the usage dashboard; fallback is spreadsheets.
Reading, representing and reporting do not change.
Committee members' time does not change.
research_questions: Is preparation time per meeting shorter?

incremental.description: Librarian checks dashboard figures before quoting them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: committees that need figures the dashboard lacks; high: committees that mostly ask standard usage figures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clarify the subject and audience, search the catalogue and databases, select and annotate items, format the list and citations, check it, and send it to the requester.

steps.what: Librarian clarifies the subject and audience for the list
Librarian searches the catalogue and databases for books, periodicals, articles and audio-visual materials

loop.input: The subject and audience, and the library's catalogue and licensed databases.
loop.output: Candidate items, each linked to a catalogue or database record.
loop.check: Code drops every item that does not resolve to a record; the librarian reviews the list.
loop.stop: One search round per brief; with no hits the librarian searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Subjects are asked in plain words that do not match subject headings.

steps.what: Librarian selects and annotates the items for the audience
Librarian formats the list and citations
Librarian checks the formatted list before it goes
Librarian e-mails the list to the requester

tasks.design: A search step over the library's own catalogue and licensed databases ({OTHER}) turns the subject into candidate items, and code keeps only items that resolve to a real record, so no invented titles get through. The librarian selects and annotates, the list and citations are formatted from the records by template, and the librarian checks the list before it goes to the requester.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each list was searched, typed and formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Library discovery tools answer subject questions from their own records with links.
tasks.still_hard: Good lists depend on judging quality, not just matching the subject.
tasks.human_edge: Leaving out the popular title that is out of date.
tasks.altitude: The librarian selects from checked candidates instead of searching from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether lists arrive in time for the course.

evidence.claim: Primo Research Assistant answers reference questions from the top five abstracts with source links.
The Library of Virginia estimates 15% of e-mailed reference questions are chatbot-generated, some citing invented works.

assumptions: Boundary: from the list request to the list sent; buying missing items is outside.
Input contract: requests from teachers or patrons; catalogue and database records; fallback is searching by hand.
Selecting and annotating stay with the librarian.
Only items with a record reach the list.
research_questions: How many candidates does the librarian keep?

incremental.description: Librarian reports irrelevant candidates to improve the search.

approvals.approved_version: The list as checked by the librarian in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: niche subjects with thin catalogue coverage; high: common subjects well covered by the catalogue and databases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The librarian keeps planning and delivering programmes, conferring and selecting; drafting texts, sign-up lists, searching and formatting shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A librarian who spends saved time in front of groups.
